title: Orbit equivalence of graph products over the same finite graph from orbit-equivalent free probability actions of corresponding vertex groups
source_title: Measure equivalence classification of transvection-free right-angled Artin groups
author: Camille Horbez; Jingyin Huang
difficulty_reason: Orbit equivalence of each vertex action does not directly produce a free action of the graph product on a common probability space. Section4 transplants the measurable vertex orbit cocycle through a graph-product retraction and checks that its variable labels preserve commutation along links. The same construction must still preserve probability measure and nontrivial reduced words, so the action/freeness construction remains a substantive obligation after the source normal-form theorem is allowed.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Independent Proposition4.2, with arbitrary countable corresponding vertex groups over the same finite simple graph, each pair admitting orbit-equivalent FREE probability-measure-preserving actions on standard probability spaces. Complete induction, unique vertex cocycle, product action, link commutation, countable Borel partition measure preservation and reduced-word proof of freeness40–41 read. Green graph-product normal form and Gaboriau orbit-equivalence-to-measure-equivalence criterion are explicit published research foundations. No transvection-free assumption is needed for this separate graph-product result; that restriction belongs to main classification. Not substituting measure equivalence for vertex orbit equivalence. No amenable special case, continuum examples, main extension-graph rigidity or nonuniform lattice claim separately selected.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: A measurable orbit cocycle is transplanted through a graph-product retraction into a product Bernoulli action; commutation along links and reduced-word freeness must survive variable cocycle labels to realize orbit equivalence of the full nonamenable graph products.
